about: How another model's own logic was merged into Vote Helper's single set of questions and mappings. These are judgment calls made when merging (by Claude, 2026-10-21), meant to be reviewed by the other model in the critique step. tools/merge-logic.js applies this file.
label: Grok

tax_progressivity.why: Same disagreement: whether the highest earners and wealthiest should pay more. The sides are swapped (Grok's side B is Vote Helper's side A).

government_size.why: Same core trade-off: more taxes and services, or less. Grok's version also mentions regulation, which Vote Helper asks about separately.

bond_debt.why: Same question about state borrowing; sides swapped.

spending_limits.why: Both ask whether good-year revenue should be locked away (reserves, limits) or kept flexible for services. Vote Helper's question is reworded to cover spending limits as well as reserves.

reword.label: Saving and spending limits
reword.q: When the state takes in extra money in good years, what should happen to it?
reword.a: Spend it on current needs, with flexibility to expand services
reword.b: Save more in reserves and keep firm limits on spending

housing_supply.why: A different question from Vote Helper's housing question (neighborhood scale vs. building more): Grok's asks how to get homes built (remove barriers vs. fund subsidized units). Both are real splits among voters, so both are kept.

new.label: How to get more housing built
new.q: To bring down housing costs, what should government focus on?
new.a: Removing rules and delays so more homes of all kinds get built
new.b: Public money and requirements for homes reserved as affordable

voting_id.why: Same question about ID and verification.

campaign_finance.why: Same question about public campaign financing; sides swapped.

ceqa_process.why: Same question: thorough environmental review vs. faster approvals.

local_tax_threshold.why: Same question about majority vs. two-thirds for local taxes; sides swapped.

party_lean.why: Same question; sides swapped. Vote Helper's wording is kept because Grok's side A grouped independents with Republicans.

recall_process.why: Same question. Vote Helper asks it only as a follow-up for Prop 5, since it concerns one measure. Grok's mapping (Yes on Prop 5 moves toward filling vacancies later) matches Vote Helper's.

education_funding.why: Asks about one measure (Prop 3: make the temporary rates permanent) rather than a general value. Prop 3 is already mapped through taxing the wealthy and taxes vs. services, where both models agree.

q_p40_flight.why: A distinct consideration for Prop 40 (whether wealthy residents would leave) that Vote Helper's follow-up doesn't ask.

q_p45_tradeoff.why: Asks the same thing as the environmental review question.

q_ins_race.why: Asks which candidate's background you prefer, which the experience question and the public-insurance follow-up already cover.

p38#0.why: Same concern: half the bond goes to one institute.

p40#0.why: New: valuing hard-to-price assets invites valuation disputes and lawsuits.

p40#1.why: Same concern: Props 41 and 42 can cancel it.

p44#0.why: Same concern: what counts as qualifying spending is open-ended.

p45#0.why: New: covers a very broad set of projects and narrows public comment and court review.

stances.why: Where a model gives every candidate in a race the same value on a question (e.g. two Democrats on party lean), it has no effect and is left out.
